summary: Ten sector-specific guide concepts have individual evidence screens. They are provisional and not qualified; the 2022 U.S. NAICS classifications and adjacent Korn Ferry pages define context, not KOV demand or candidate-side SERP opportunity.
programme_note: Ten additional sector-specific URLs have individual provisional research records and blueprints, bringing industry-guide candidates to 13 of 45. All remain unqualified pending direct candidate-SERP, demand, serviceability, and overlap review; 32 quota slots remain unassigned.
quota_and_next_batch: The industry-specific guide quota is 45. Ten concepts were added to the three earlier cross-industry candidates, for 13 individually screened URLs and 32 unassigned quota slots. No candidate is qualified for development. Next: examine the existing sector pages and first-party query evidence; prioritize only cases with a demonstrably separate candidate task and verified KOV serviceability.

candidate_defaults.search_intent: Informational career exploration: understand leadership roles, employer context, or transferable evidence in {industry_name}. This is a qualitative intent hypothesis; query demand has not been measured.
intent_evidence: The 2022 NAICS workbook supplies U.S. industry classifications for the listed codes. Classification confirms sector terminology only; it is not evidence that people search for this candidate page.
candidate_defaults.geographic_relevance: The cited NAICS codes are U.S. classifications. English-language framing may be broader, but labor markets, regulation, role scope, and KOV serviceability have not been established outside the relevant jurisdiction.

candidate_defaults.commercial_relevance: May support KOV's candidate-side role and industry navigation if the proposed content is differentiated and serviceable. No placement capability, industry coverage, demand, or conversion value is inferred from taxonomy or a competitor consulting page.
candidate_defaults.unique_content_purpose: If later qualified, {title} would explain {unique_angle} for senior professionals. It must add candidate-facing career context beyond the existing broad sector page and must not imply KOV offers services or placements in this industry.
candidate_defaults.overlap_assessment: The existing site has a broad sector route at {existing_industry_hub}. {overlap_note} Keep a standalone URL only if it answers a distinct candidate task, has verified KOV serviceability, and is supported by first-party demand evidence. The NAICS classification is U.S.-specific.
factual_gaps_and_risks: Verify the listed NAICS codes and labels against the local 2022 Census workbook before publication; classification does not establish a career-content need.
Review the full existing sector hub at {existing_industry_hub}, relevant role pages, and current public copy for overlap.
Validate candidate-side search intent and competitor pages with actual location-appropriate Google/Bing results; no SERP ranking evidence is recorded here.
No Search Console, keyword volume, difficulty, traffic, or conversion evidence is available.
Confirm that KOV can accurately serve and discuss the audience and jurisdiction; do not imply sector-specific placement services.
proposed_outline: Define the audience and the employer/industry scope for {title}; state the U.S. NAICS codes as classification references, not a global taxonomy.
Explain the sector-specific operating context relevant to senior-role scope, using current reliable evidence before drafting.
Separate transferable leadership evidence from industry-specific knowledge or requirements; avoid promising transition outcomes.
Link to the current KOV sector hub, role strategy, and market guide only where relevant.

candidates.title: Biotechnology and Pharmaceutical Leadership Careers
candidates.naics_names: Research and Development in Biotechnology (except Nanobiotechnology); Pharmaceutical Preparation Manufacturing
candidates.audience: Senior biotechnology, pharmaceutical, R&D, and commercial professionals exploring leadership roles across research, development, and commercialization.
candidates.unique_angle: the R&D-to-commercial handoff and product lifecycle across biotechnology and pharmaceutical employers
candidates.competitor_finding: The page treats biotechnology, medical devices/diagnostics, and pharmaceuticals as distinct segments and discusses R&D, talent strategy, and leadership solutions; it is an organizational consulting reference rather than a candidate guide.
candidates.overlap_note: Healthcare and manufacturing are broad existing sectors. Differentiate only around life-sciences operating models and career transitions, not a rebranded sector overview.

candidates.title: Medical Device and Diagnostics Leadership Careers
candidates.audience: Senior product, quality, regulatory, commercial, and operations professionals targeting medical-device or diagnostics employers.
candidates.unique_angle: the interface among technical products, regulation, clinical adoption, and senior operating responsibility
candidates.competitor_finding: The page identifies Medical Devices & Diagnostics as a distinct life-sciences segment and discusses talent strategy and leadership development; it does not provide candidate-side career guidance.
candidates.overlap_note: Healthcare and manufacturing coverage already exists. Require device-specific candidate content and verify the full current pages before keeping a separate URL.

candidates.title: Semiconductor and Technology-Systems Leadership Careers
candidates.audience: Senior engineering, operations, product, supply-chain, and commercial professionals exploring semiconductor leadership.
candidates.unique_angle: the capital-intensive operating model, fab operations, specialized supply chains, and leadership evidence of semiconductor businesses
candidates.competitor_finding: The page addresses semiconductor and high-technology leadership, talent, and organizational needs. It is a close industry-services reference but not a candidate-facing career guide.
candidates.overlap_note: Technology and manufacturing pages overlap. A distinct guide would need semiconductor-specific leadership context rather than broad technology or manufacturing copy.

candidates.title: Data Center and Cloud-Infrastructure Leadership Careers

candidates.competitor_finding: The page discusses talent and leadership in digital infrastructure and telecommunications but is broader than data centers/cloud infrastructure; treat it as adjacent context only.
candidates.overlap_note: The concept spans technology, utilities, and real estate and risks crossing multiple existing hubs. Define the employer segment precisely and inspect all related sector pages.
